extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: CONTEXTUAL is a benchmark dataset featuring 506 human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive joint reasoning over textual and visual elements in text-rich images. It spans eight real-world visual scenarios: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., & Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. In Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024), PMLR 235.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from six distinct sources: LAION-5B via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories; Rico Dataset for Application Usage; Open WebText Initiative URL scraping for Web Usage; InfographicVQA for Infographics; and STVQA and ESTVQA for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes. Human instructions and reference responses were authored by the study's researchers across the categories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LAION-5B, Rico Dataset (Android app UI screens), Open WebText Initiative (scraped webpage screenshots), InfographicVQA test set, STVQA test set, and ESTVQA test set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images categorized under Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract underwent manual filtering to guarantee suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, heuristic filtering was applied using PaddleOCR to detect text and select the top 500 images with the highest number of words before annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: In Stage 2, authors were split into two groups, each annotating four categories to create <image, instruction, response> triplets following guidelines requiring context-sensitive joint reasoning. In Stage 3, Amazon Mechanical Turk workers verified sample correctness (finding 96% correct), incorrect samples were filtered out, and author groups cross-reviewed each other's samples to yield the final 506 instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers verified the correctness of each annotated <image, instruction, response> sample; 96% of the samples were verified as correct, and incorrect samples were filtered out. Each author group also cross-reviewed samples created by the other group.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Mainly from the US (for the human response baseline / evaluation tasks on Amazon Mechanical Turk).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples from the 506 is released as a validation set along with reference responses, while reference responses are kept hidden for the remaining 406 samples. A continuously updated leaderboard is maintained on HuggingFace.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed in the dataset. Models evaluated on the dataset hallucinated, but no harmful or privacy-sensitive information was present in the benchmark items.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables evaluation and advancement of Large Multimodal Models in context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning tasks with real-world applications, such as assisting the visually impaired in navigating public spaces and interpreting digital/physical text-rich environments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Annotators providing baseline responses and human evaluations were mainly from the US, potentially reflecting specific linguistic diversity and writing style biases. Pretraining data imbalances in foundation models towards natural scenes over digital scenes were also highlighted.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human baseline and human evaluation rely predominantly on US-based annotators, which may affect linguistic diversity and writing style; annotating context-sensitive text-rich instructions is time-consuming and difficult to crowdsource on a budget; models tested display limitations in fine-grained visual perception, handling time-related data, and interpreting infographics.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating the context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and augmented Large Language Models (LLMs).
